task_label: Implement semantic routine reuse from natural user phrasing
problem_statement: The technical runner can execute by generated routine name or explicit trigger phrase, but product acceptance must not require users to remember names like `Routine List Events`. After saving a routine from a natural calendar+weather request, Janus must recognize a later semantically matching natural request and use the saved routine.

latest_user_evidence.actual: The proposed acceptance retest asked the user to type `Routine List Events`, which the user rejected as bad UX.
latest_user_evidence.expected: The user repeats the natural request, for example `Was steht heute in meinem Kalender und wie wird das Wetter in Koeln?`; Janus finds the saved calendar+weather routine, runs it, and says it used the routine.

acceptance_criteria: Only allowlisted backend routine/intent/orchestrator files and focused tests may change.

A saved routine with steps `calendar.list_events` then `system.weather` must execute when a later natural request asks for calendar plus weather, even when the routine name or generated trigger phrase is not present.
Existing explicit trigger phrase execution must still pass.
An unrelated natural request must not execute the routine.
The successful routine response must transparently say that a saved or matching routine was used.
Do not add UI, transport APIs, OAuth, product OpenRouter, Memory Session-Search, embeddings, migration, Git, or broad architecture changes.
cursor_prompt_contract: Use Cursor Composer for one bounded execution patch. Inspect only allowlisted files, implement the smallest safe semantic routine reuse matcher, run listed checks, and return concise JSON-compatible output.
